newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine foreign investment $1.4 bln since '91-govt.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine foreign investment $1.4 bln since '91-govt.

text.p: Private foreign investment in Ukraine has totalled $1.4 billion dollars since independence in 1991, with investment in January of this year alone some $458.9 million, the Statistics Ministry said on Friday.

The largest investors have been the U.S.($245.3 million), Germany ($182.9 million), Netherlands ($119.2 million), Russia ($114.1 million), Britain ($94.8 million) and Cyprus ($72.9 million), the ministry said.
Cyprus is a popular offshore centre for Russian investors.
A total of 5,263 businesses have some form of foreign investment, it said, and 4,117 businesses are foreign investment joint-ventures.
Most businesses with foreign investment are involved in trade, followed by light manufacturing, machine-building and metals.

Government officials have said Ukraine needs $40 billion in foreign investment to push ahead significantly with economic reforms. Foreign investors have complained about problems with corruption, punitive taxes and unpredictable laws.
Ukrainian foreign investment, mainly in other former Soviet republics, has totalled about $82.7 million since independence.
